title: Five Discoveries That Changed How We Picture T. Rex
summary:
Tyrannosaurus rex has been famous since it was named in 1905. Paleontologists are still updating the picture of this Cretaceous predator, from how it looked to how it lived.

Early ideas showed a slow, swamp-dwelling giant with a dragging tail. Cassius Morrison, a paleontologist at University College London, says that older view imagined continuous battles among sluggish dinosaurs. Newer research paints T. rex as more active and warm-blooded, possibly with feathers, and as an animal that both hunted and scavenged.

One long puzzle was its tiny arms. Scientists once wondered why such a large hunter had such small forelimbs. Fossils of related dinosaurs and a T. rex forearm found in 1988 showed it had two fingers, not three. A study of theropod arms published in May argued the small arms were a tradeoff: a huge, powerful head needed space for neck muscles, and oversized arms would have made the animal too front-heavy.

Teeth are another update. Many movies show T. rex with teeth always visible. A 2023 study of a close relative suggested lips may have covered the teeth when the mouth was closed, helping protect enamel, more like some modern lizards than crocodiles that live much of their lives in water.

How T. rex hunted is still debated. Research indicates it was not a long-distance sprinter—top speed estimates are around 12 miles per hour—but it could turn well and likely used short bursts as an ambush hunter. Tooth marks in healed bones suggest it attacked living prey, while bone fragments in fossil dung show it also ate large carcasses.

Scientists also study body temperature and metabolism to estimate how much food such a giant needed. Together, these findings keep rewriting the story of the “tyrant lizard king.”
why_it_matters: Famous dinosaurs are good examples of how science updates old ideas with new evidence. Learning that pictures change helps kids treat museum stories as living research, not fixed cartoons.

Scientific pictures of famous dinosaurs change when new fossils and studies appear.
